dimensions.assessment: Affects Department of Justice personnel and leadership associated with the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
dimensions.evidence: There is hereby established a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice under the authority of the Attorney General

dimensions.assessment: Codifies an existing internal DOJ division and establishes a presidentially designated Assistant Attorney General position.
dimensions.evidence: The National Fraud Enforcement Division was established by DOJ in April 2026.

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply specific federal spending, revenue, or economic effects.
Amends title 28 and title 5 of the United States Code to provide statutory grounding and ethical restrictions for the division and its head.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 31 of title 28, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 509B the following: Sec. 509C. National Fraud Enforcement Division

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory office within the Department of Justice.
dimensions.evidence: There is hereby established a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice

missing_information: Budget allocations or staffing numbers for the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill provides statutory authority for the National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice, which was previously established administratively by the DOJ in April 2026.

Res. 213) providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the ‘‘California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision''; and providing for consideration of the Senate amendments to the bill (H.R. 5334) to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes.
